subject: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme

Evan —

Quick update and immediate action items from our side. We detected a partial peering degradation into our EU routing fabric starting 08:00 UTC that is intermittently impacting TLS handshake times and connection establishment for a subset of tenants (including Acme). Our automated fallbacks kicked in but we’re seeing persistent connection-level timeouts for some long-lived socket clients.

What we can do right now (two options):
1) Customer-initiated — fastest for you: toggle the account-level geo-bridge in your Console (Console link below). This will direct traffic to the EU bridge cluster across an alternate egress path we’ve brought online.
2) Redwood-managed — we can opt Acme in from our side (recommended if you prefer us to act). We’ll flip the account flag and push a short-lived header that prefers the bridge.

Temporary test steps (if you want to validate quickly):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" -H "x-redwood-geo-prefer: eu-bridge" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
- Run a quick generate request (1 token) and look for "x-redwood-routing: eu-bridge" in response headers.

Expected behavior and impact:
- Failover latency: initial requests may see an extra 150–350ms during the first handshake as K/V cache warms.
- No model switching — same model and version; just alternate egress path.
- Billing: usage continues as normal; no credit changes.

Attachments: eu-bridge-topology.png (network diagram), acme-reroute-checklist.pdf (validation steps).

Please reply with which option you prefer. If we don’t hear back in 30 minutes we’ll proceed with the Redwood-managed opt-in to minimize disruption.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Platform Team <ops@acme.com>
Date: 2029-03-05T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the quick note. Can you confirm if the Redwood-managed opt-in will cause any client-side changes for our engineering team? We’d prefer Redwood to handle this if it’s seamless. Also can you confirm the expected window and how we validate end-to-end?

Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform
Acme Corp

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-05T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme

Sofia / Laura —

Please approve Redwood-managed opt-in for Acme. We have pre-validated account-level changes for all enterprise tenants and the change is a single flag flip in the control plane (no SDK or DNS changes required). Engineering (Connor) will run the bridge-init sequence and monitor L7 latency while we flip the account.

Steps I’ll execute once approved:
- Flag set on Account ACME-009 (control plane)
- Trigger bridge-init on eu-bridge-03 (expected ~45s warm-up)
- Smoke test against api.redwood-inference.com with x-redwood-geo-prefer header to validate routing
- Notify customer and keep the flag in place until handoff (we’ll provide exact timestamps and logs)

Note: we expect an initial token spike due to re-auth handshakes; we’ll watch billing metrics but don’t anticipate billing anomalies. Tracker: HUBSPOT-43219.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-05T08:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme

On 2029-03-05 08:31, Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> Please approve Redwood-managed opt-in for Acme. We have pre-validated account-level changes for all enterprise tenants and the change is a single flag flip in the control plane (no SDK or DNS changes required).
> — Vanessa Ortiz

Evan — we will proceed with Redwood-managed opt-in now per Vanessa’s recommendation. No action required on your side.

What to expect in the next 6 minutes:
- We will flip the account-level flag and trigger bridge-init. You may see a few 502/503s during the handshake window if you have long-lived streaming connections — normal and do not indicate data loss.
- Validation steps for you: run the curl above and confirm you see "x-redwood-routing: eu-bridge". Also paste any failing request ids to this thread and we’ll pull traces.
- Post-action: we’ll leave the bridge in place for 24 hours while we monitor. If you’d like to opt out earlier, reply and we’ll revert.

We will also share a post-incident timeline and packet-level traces in the follow-up (scheduled call below).

Sofia

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-05T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo access bridge: immediate reroute instructions for Acme

Bridge-init completed for Account ACME-009 on eu-bridge-03 at 09:03:12-07:00.

Quick notes:
- Observability: initial L7 handshake latency dropped from 2.1s to 310ms for traffic routed over eu-bridge-03.
- Smoke tests: 10/10 generate requests returned with x-redwood-routing: eu-bridge.
- Attachments uploaded to ticket: acme-reroute-checklist.pdf, eu-bridge-topology.png.

I left the flag in place and set a 24-hour monitoring window. We’ll compile the postmortem and timeline by EOD and schedule the customer call for 14:00 UTC today (calendar invite to follow).

— Connor Obrien
SRE, Redwood Inference
